subject: Clarify: Hosted API expected monthly tokens & burst TPS — Vectra discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@vectra.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: Hosted API expected monthly tokens & burst TPS — Vectra discovery follow-up

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. I promised a short written recap and a couple of specific asks so we can finalize a pricing sketch for procurement. Below is what I heard; please flag anything off.

Summary of what we discussed
- Primary use: in-product assistant + backend summarization for support tickets.
- Expected steady-state: ~35M tokens / month across a mix of short prompts and multi-turn sessions (avg response length ~120 tokens).
- Peak/burst: estimated 400 concurrent requests during marketing-driven spikes; we approximated this maps to ~180 QPS / ~3k tokens/sec at peak.
- Latency target: 95th <= 250ms for short completions, ~500ms acceptable for long-form summaries.
- Data/safety: standard SOC2 + allowed PII (redaction on our side).

Clarifying asks (so pricing sheet aligns)
1) Can you confirm the expected monthly token range as a 3-point estimate (low/most-likely/high)? Your team mentioned seasonality so a range helps us pick the right commit tier.
2) For the peak shape: is the 400 concurrent a sustained level for >10 minutes or a short 1–2 minute spike? This affects how we model burst capacity and reserve pools.
3) Any constraints from procurement on minimum term or payment cadence? (monthly vs quarterly vs annual)

Requested next steps
- If you confirm the three-point token estimate and whether the 400 concurrent is short vs sustained, I’ll send an initial pricing sketch (token $/1M tiers + burst add-on) and a draft SOW for review.
- If procurement prefers, I can loop in our finance lead for a quick alignment call — suggest Tue/Wed next week.

Attachments: I’ll attach a one-page pricing matrix and a starter SOW in my next message.

Thanks — speaking plainly on economics will speed approvals on both sides.

Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Alex Morgan <alex@vectra.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <contracts@vectra.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: Hosted API expected monthly tokens & burst TPS — Vectra discovery follow-up

Thanks Mina — appreciate the tidy recap. Quick answers inline: 

1) Monthly token range (three-point)
- Low: 20M (minimal pilot with support only)
- Most likely: 36–40M (what we'll likely settle into after Q4)
- High: 60M (campaigns + new feature launch in Nov)

2) Peak shape
- The 400 concurrent is usually a short burst (1–3 minutes) triggered by email blasts / homepage traffic. We do have a few longer spikes during special events (~10–15 minutes) but those are infrequent (2–3x/year).

3) Procurement preferences
- They prefer quarterly invoicing; no strict annual minimum but they are open to term discounts if commit >12 months.

Happy for you to send the pricing sketch and SOW. If useful, procurement is available Wed afternoon for a quick sync (they're CC'd).

— Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product, Vectra Analytics
alex@vectra.ai | +1 (303) 555-8812

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: Hosted API expected monthly tokens & burst TPS — Vectra discovery follow-up

Perfect — that helps a lot. Based on your ranges we’ll draft two pricing options:
A) Pilot-to-production (quarterly billing): 6-month ramp, commit to 30M/mo nominal with a pay-as-you-go overage bucket. Target price: $28 / 1M tokens on standard gen model; burst buffer priced as fixed $/minute for reserve capacity during 1–3 minute spikes.
B) Committed annual (term discount): 12-month commit at an average of 45M/mo steady-state — target blended price: $21 / 1M tokens with an included monthly burst allowance up to 300 QPS, excess billed per-minute.

I attached a simple pricing matrix and a starter SOW (SOW-draft-v1.pdf, pricing-sheet.csv) for internal review. These are strawman numbers so we can move procurement quickly.

Proposed next steps
- Procurement sync Wed 22 Jun 15:00 PT (if that works) — Vanessa, Marissa: can you join and cover committed terms + legal handoff?
- Alex: after procurement alignment, we’ll prepare a formal term sheet and sample invoice cadence.

On quotas/ops: Vanessa — short note below on burst handling (cc’d).

Thanks,
Mina

Subject: Re: Clarify: Hosted API expected monthly tokens & burst TPS — Vectra discovery follow-up

Alex / team — thanks for confirming the shape. A few operational notes so procurement has clarity going into the call: 

- Burst behavior: for short 1–3 minute spikes we recommend a cost-effective burst buffer (pre-warmed capacity) charged as a fixed hourly/minute rate rather than per-token to avoid token-price churn during spikes. For the rare 10–15 minute sustained events we suggest temporary autoscale credits (one-off invoice line) or an agreed upper-tier burst pool with minute granularity.
- Invoicing cadence: we can support quarterly invoices; we'll include a monthly usage statement itemizing token counts by model and request type.
- Contract clauses to expect: standard SLAs for uptime; a 30-day notice for model changes that materially affect latency/cost; data handling and retention specifics (SOC2 clause).

Marissa — can you bring a draft of the term/discount schedule to Wed’s call (I’ll send a calendar invite for 15:00 PT)? Alex — if procurement needs to invite legal, please loop them into that invite.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
